name: Diagonal Roll Repair (Rolling Out-and-Up / Out-and-Down)
summary: Convert a tested vertical or short option into a diagonal by buying back the tested short and selling a further-out expiry at a better strike; the standard defensive transformation that creates most real-world diagonals.

legs.strike_rule: Buy back the existing tested short at its current strike (closing leg).

Sell a new short at a strike further from spot, chosen by delta 0.20-0.30, and still on the covered side of the existing long (for calls: new short strike > long strike; for puts: new short strike < long strike).
legs.dte_rule: a LATER expiry, 21-45 DTE, but STRICTLY BEFORE the existing long leg's expiry

max_profit: The original structure's max profit plus the new net credit, minus any loss already realized on the closing leg. Each valid roll raises the cumulative credit.
max_loss: Whatever the resulting diagonal's max loss is: net debit for a debit diagonal, or (strike width x 100 - cumulative credit) for a credit diagonal. The roll must never increase max loss.
breakevens: Recompute from the new structure; each credit roll improves the breakeven by the credit per share.

greeks.delta: reduced in magnitude by moving the short strike away from spot
greeks.gamma: reduced by moving to a later expiry
greeks.theta: slightly reduced per day but extended over more days
greeks.vega: increased slightly because the new short is further out in time

when_to_use: When a short leg has been tested (|delta| >= 0.50) but the underlying thesis is intact and there is a later expiry where a strike further from spot can be sold for a NET CREDIT. It is the standard way a covered call becomes a PMCC-style diagonal and a vertical becomes a bull/bear diagonal.
typical_dte: new short 21-45 DTE, always earlier than the long leg's expiry
entry_rules: Only roll for a NET CREDIT. If the roll costs a debit, close the position instead - paying to stay in a losing trade is the most expensive habit in options.

VALIDATION (must be enforced on every roll): the new short's expiry must be STRICTLY EARLIER than the covering long's expiry. Rolling past the long's expiry silently creates a reverse diagonal and an uncovered short.
VALIDATION: for calls, new short strike >= long strike + cumulative net debit; for puts, new short strike <= long strike - cumulative net debit.
New short delta 0.20-0.30; never roll into a strike that is still ITM.
Maximum 3 rolls per position. After the third, close regardless.
The roll must not increase the position's maximum loss - if it does, reject and close.
LEVEL 3 OK provided both validations pass. Execute as a single 2-leg mleg (buy-to-close + sell-to-open) so the account is never momentarily naked.
management_rules: Track cumulative credits; every subsequent strike constraint uses the running net debit or credit, not the original.
If the position requires a fourth roll, the thesis is wrong - close it.
After any roll, re-verify the covering relationship (strike and expiry) programmatically before the next session.
If the underlying has moved more than 2 ATR against the position since entry, do not roll - close.
exit_rules: The closing side of the roll must fill before or simultaneously with the opening side; if the mleg does not fill as a package, BUY TO CLOSE first and only then sell the new short.
If no credit roll exists that satisfies both validations, close the entire structure by 14:30 ET on the short's expiration day.
Close the short immediately if extrinsic <= $0.05 or |delta| >= 0.90 rather than attempting a roll into the last hour.
Never roll on expiration day after 14:00 ET - liquidity is poor and assignment risk is immediate. Close instead.
assignment_risk: During the roll, if executed as two separate orders in the wrong sequence, the account can be momentarily naked. Always buy to close first. The rolled-into short carries the ordinary front-leg assignment risk and the same ex-dividend and extrinsic-value rules apply.
buying_power: Unchanged or reduced if the roll widens the distance to spot; a roll that widens the strike width on a credit structure INCREASES the requirement and must be checked before submission.
liquidity_needs: The target expiry must be liquid enough to sell into: OI >= 300, spread <= $0.05 on the new short.
common_mistakes: Rolling for a debit; rolling past the long leg's expiry (creating a naked short); rolling a third and fourth time to avoid booking a loss; rolling on expiration afternoon into an illiquid market; forgetting to re-check the strike constraint against the running net debit.
zero_dte_notes: Do not roll a 0DTE short into a later expiry after 14:00 ET; close it.
family: Calendar and diagonal spreads (time spreads): same-strike calendars, different-strike diagonals, double/triple calendars, double diagonals, PMCC and its put mirror, LEAPS diagonals, calendarized straddles/butterflies, ratio time spreads, and the reverse (short) time spreads
